items.stem: Why can a convenience sample not support claims about the whole population?

options.text: It is self-selected, so it is not representative and has unknown bias
options.rationale: Correct: non-probability samples cannot be generalised reliably.
Size is not the core issue; representativeness is.

options.text: It has no sampling error at all
options.rationale: It has bias that a margin of error cannot fix.

options.rationale: Correct: double-barrelled questions cannot be answered cleanly.

options.text: A leading question that suggests a preferred answer
A single, neutral question with a balanced scale

options.rationale: A clear time reference improves a question.

items.stem: A survey reports 62% support. What makes this honest?

options.text: Reporting it with a margin of error, e.g. 62% plus or minus 3 points
options.rationale: Correct: a margin of error conveys the estimate's precision.

options.text: Stating 62% as an exact, certain figure
options.rationale: That overstates precision and hides sampling error.

options.text: Dropping the sample size from the report

options.rationale: Rounding does not address the missing margin of error.
